description: main is what has been released and develop is where work lands (docs/box.md, "Where a release lives"). Renovate feeds the release train, and main takes nothing else: the chart's app images on main only, whose patch and digest bumps merge themselves once CI is green, and the platform pins on both branches, one pull request per pin, whose patch bumps on main merge themselves once CI is green (k0s excepted: no CI job installs it). Nothing merges itself on develop, from any file. What merges itself is merged by Renovate, not GitHub's auto-merge (platformAutomerge off): neither branch requires a status check, so GitHub would merge the moment a pull request is mergeable, before CI has run, where Renovate merges only once every check on the branch is green. The sums bot is listed in gitIgnoredAuthors: it commits k0s's asset checksums onto Renovate's own k0s branch, and without that listing Renovate reads the commit as another author's edit -- it stops committing to the branch, and the pull request is left alone.

customManagers.description: Every version box installs: charts/s5n/platform.yaml. The pins ship in the chart, so a platform bump is a chart release, and box reads them from the release it pulled. One key per component, and the comment on the line names the datasource and package the version comes from, so a bump is one line in one file and CI's e2e tests exactly what ships. The shape is flat and the marker inline because both readers are then trivial: this regex here, and `sed` in the e2e (no YAML parser on the host). A value may be a whole image reference (`repository:tag@sha256:...`, which is the login's pin): the second pattern takes those, with the repository as depName, the tag as currentValue and the digest as currentDigest, so Renovate bumps the tag and its digest together. The first pattern refuses a colon in its value, so a reference never reaches it as a version Renovate cannot compare.

Every app image the chart blesses: charts/s5n/variants.yaml. The chart owns the file, ships it inside the archive, and generates the admission policy's blessed-repository list from it, so a bump here is how a new app image reaches a seedbox. Renovate's helm-values manager reads only values.yaml, so nothing else watches this file: one app per block, repository/tag/digest on three lines, and the digest is captured too so a tag and its digest move together. The s5n entry does not match: its digest is empty (the chart stamps it at packaging), so it never looks like a sha256 to bump.

Test-only images the e2e runs, pinned by tag and digest in the scripts: box never installs them, so they stay where they are used. The `# renovate: datasource=docker` marker is what keeps Renovate off the e2e's own locally built image, which is tagged, never pinned.

packageRules.description: main takes only the chart's two pin files, the app images (variants.yaml) and the platform pins (platform.yaml): they are what a release ships, and a bump to one is a chart release. Everything else -- Go modules, GitHub Actions, the Dockerfile, the test-only images in hack/ -- is code, and code reaches main through develop and a release, never as a pull request to main of its own. This rule switches every update off on main and the next one switches the two files back on: in Renovate the later matching rule wins.
The two files main does take (see the rule above).

The app images are main only: develop gets them through the back-merge after each release, never as a pull request of its own, so a develop branch is never ahead of the images users run. A custom manager cannot be scoped to a base branch, so the rule disables this file on develop rather than the manager: the nearest Renovate allows, and it leaves the platform pins (which both branches want) alone.

The chart's app images are exactly what the kind e2e installs, so on main every patch or digest bump that lands in one window goes into one pull request and merges itself as soon as the checks are green: CI runs the full e2e on them, and the push that carries it cuts the chart release. Grouping is the batching -- there is no schedule to tune.

The qBittorrent build compiled for AMD Zen 3 is the one image the e2e cannot run: it dies with SIGILL on CI's runners and most hosts, and it is amd64 only. So a green run says nothing about its new bytes, and it never merges itself, patch or digest. It gets a pull request of its own: a group merges itself only when every update in it may, so inside the app images group it would hold every other image back. This rule sits after the app images one because the later matching rule wins, and its tag is where the build profile is named (5.3.0-lt1.2-10g-znver3-mimalloc).

A minor or major app image bump changes an app's behaviour, and the e2e proves the images, not the release notes: it gets its own pull request (no groupName, so it never joins the app images one) and waits for the maintainer, who cuts the release that ships it.

The platform pins are bumped on both branches, so work on develop is built and tested against the platform it will ship on. One pull request per pin: no groupName here on purpose, because a bad cert-manager and a bad k0s are different questions and the maintainer reads them one at a time. Patch bumps on main merge themselves through the next rule.

Platform pin patch bumps on main merge themselves once CI is green: hack/e2e-box.sh runs in CI and installs the platform through box (Envoy Gateway, MetalLB, cert-manager and the login; not k0s, since kind stands in for the cluster), so a green run tests exactly the pins that ship, and the push that carries the merge cuts the chart patch release. The authelia line's digest moves with its tag, so a patch covers it. A minor or major bump (MetalLB is still 0.x) always waits for the maintainer. k0s is excluded by the next rule, which must stay after this one: in Renovate the later matching rule wins.

A k0s bump never merges itself, and this rule sits after the platform patch rule so it wins over it. No CI job installs k0s: hack/e2e-box.sh runs on kind, which stands in for the cluster, so a green run says nothing about a new k0s. .github/workflows/k0s-sums.yaml writes the asset checksums Renovate cannot (as the sums bot, whose App token push starts CI where a GITHUB_TOKEN one would not), so the pull request can go green; a maintainer still merges it. Patch bumps join the platform automerge when an e2e that boots k0s runs in CI; a k0s minor is a Kubernetes minor and always waits.
A test-only image in hack/ changes what the e2e runs, never what box ships: it is never automerged, whatever a preset later says.

No hourly limit anywhere (the top-level 0s replace config:recommended's two an hour): main takes only the chart's pins, which are what users run, and its patch bumps merge themselves once CI is green, so holding them back buys nothing. develop takes everything else -- Go modules, GitHub Actions, the test images -- which can arrive twenty at once, and every pull request runs the full e2e, so at most five are open there at a time: the next opens as one merges or closes.
Nothing ever merges itself on develop, from any file, whatever a rule above says: develop is where a change is read before it is released. This rule is last so it wins.
